subject.title: Bug: OAuth token exchange silently proceeds without client_secret + hardcoded redirect port

question: Should Google/Gemini OAuth treat a missing client_secret as supported public-client PKCE behavior, a warning-only misconfiguration, or a fail-closed confidential-client error?
rationale: The current code and docs allow optional client secrets in multiple Google OAuth paths, but the report raises a real auth/security boundary that automation should not change without maintainer intent.

options.title: Document and diagnose public-client support
options.body: Keep optional client_secret support but make the mode explicit in docs/errors and warn when a confidential-client setup appears incomplete.

options.title: Fail closed without client_secret
options.body: Reject token exchange when a Google OAuth flow lacks client_secret, accepting a compatibility break for public-client or env-client-id-only setups.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Leave optional client_secret behavior unchanged and rely on Google token endpoint failures plus existing credential extraction for misconfigured setups.

recommendation.title: Document and diagnose public-client support
recommendation.body: Keep optional client_secret support but make the mode explicit in docs/errors and warn when a confidential-client setup appears incomplete.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal on the Google OAuth module split and current central files.
